newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Commission seeks to cut cost of fishing accords.
newsitem.headline: Commission seeks to cut cost of fishing accords.

text.p: Member states must consider various options for reducing the cost of European Union fishing agreements with foreign countries, the European Commission said.
The warning was contained in a report presented by Fisheries Commissioner Emma Bonino to EU fisheries ministers in Luxembourg this week.
During the past 20 years the EU has concluded 26 fishing agreements -- 15 with African and Indian ocean countries, 10 with north Atlantic countries and one with a Latin Amereican country (Argentina).
In 1996 the total cost of the agreements, allowing the capture of 132,000 tonnes of fish annually, amounted to 280 million ecus.

The various options outlined in the report were: - Reduction in the size of the EU fleet fishing in foreign waters. Extra EU aid would be needed to compensate fishermen for laying up vessels and finding other employment. It would also increase the EU's dependence on fish imports -- the EU already imports 54 percent of its fish needs. - End the less attractive fishing agreements whose opportunities are not fully exploited by fishermen and concentrate financial resources on the more economically important ones. - Fishing nations should finance a greater share of the cost of the fishing agreements.
